readings: Take fee records with a fee rate (`feerate`) strictly greater than 0.0009 and match each to its order (`fees.orderslink` = `orders.recordvault`, exact text match; drop fees with no matching order). For each combination of `orderslink` and order side (`dealedge`), compute the average net fee rate (`feerate` minus `rebrate`, ignoring missing values) and the number of records. Then compute each side's average of those group averages. List the groups whose average net fee rate is strictly greater than their side's average. Show `orderslink`, side, the group's average net fee rate, its record count, and the group average minus the side average. Sort by that difference from highest to lowest (missing last), keep the top 10, and don't round anything.
queries:
WITH g AS (
  SELECT f.orderslink AS orderslink,
         o.dealedge AS side,
         AVG(f.feerate - f.rebrate) AS avg_net,
         COUNT(*) AS cnt
  FROM fees f
  JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault
  WHERE f.feerate > 0.0009
  GROUP BY f.orderslink, o.dealedge
),
s AS (
  SELECT side, AVG(avg_net) AS side_avg
  FROM g
  GROUP BY side
)
SELECT g.orderslink, g.side, g.avg_net, g.cnt, g.avg_net - s.side_avg AS diff
FROM g
JOIN s ON g.side = s.side
WHERE g.avg_net > s.side_avg
ORDER BY diff DESC
LIMIT 10;
